purpose: Toremifene is used to treat breast cancer in women who have gone through menopause, specifically a type called estrogen receptor-positive (ER-positive) breast cancer. It works best for cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. Your doctor prescribed it because your cancer cells use estrogen to grow, and this medicine helps block that process.
how_it_works: Some breast cancer cells have special receivers called estrogen receptors that grab onto estrogen and use it as fuel to grow. Toremifene acts like a decoy — it attaches to those same receivers so estrogen cannot get in. Without estrogen's signal, the cancer cells slow down and stop growing. Think of it like putting the wrong key in a lock so the real key cannot open it.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes, sweating, nausea, dizziness, vaginal discharge or dryness, swelling in your legs or feet, and feeling tired are the most common side effects. Some women also notice changes in their mood or mild bone or joint pain. Most of these are manageable, so let your pharmacist or doctor know if anything bothers you.
warnings: Toremifene can cause a serious heart rhythm problem called QT prolongation, which can be dangerous, especially if you already take certain other medicines. Tell your doctor about all your medications before starting. It can also raise the risk of blood clots, so report any leg pain, swelling, chest pain, or trouble breathing right away. Women with a history of certain heart or liver conditions should use it with caution. This medicine should NOT be used if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 60 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to keep a steady level in your body. If you miss a dose, skip it and take the next one at your regular time — do not double up.
